title: fix(aws-lambda): serve microsoft office files as binary in lambda handler
body:
This PR fixes https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/4468

# Description:
When serving Microsoft Office files, due to the existence of "xml" as part of the mimetype, the function `defaultIsContentTypeBinary` incorrectly classifies the response as plain text and not binary. Leading to a broken file download to the user.

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code

issues.title: Lambda handler doesn't serve Office files (Excel etc) as binary
issues.body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.10.1

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

AWS Lambda

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Serve a response with the Content Type `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`. The lambda handler will incorrectly detect it as a plain text response (due to the string "xml" that's part of that mime type) and therefore the file will be broken on download at the user.

### What is the expected behavior?

Treat the response as a binary file instead of text

### What do you see instead?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

evidence.body:
Thank you for considering the changes.

As indicated in #4470, I believe we should make the following changes, including improvements to the current regular expression.

```suggestion
  return !/^text\/(?:plain|html|css|javascript|csv)|(?:\/|\+)(?:json|xml)(?:;|$)/test(
```
